Yāska (7th–5th century BCE [ 1 ] ) was an ancient Indian [ 2 ] grammarian [ 3 ] [ 4 ] and Vedic linguist . [ 5 ] Preceding Pāṇini (7th–4th century BCE [ 6 ] [ 7 ] [ 8 ] ), he is traditionally identified as the author of Nirukta , the discipline of " etymology " (explanation of words) within the Sanskrit grammatical tradition , and the Nighantu , the oldest proto-thesaurus in India. [ 9 ] Nirukta is one of the six Vedāṅgas (limbs of the Veda) in Hinduism . Yaska is widely regarded as the precursive founder of the discipline of what would become etymology in both the East and the West. [ 10 ]
